turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Brennan, I'll take your blood pressure before Dr Keane comes in. Sit yourself up straight for me, if you would.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly. Thank you.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): One forty-eight over ninety-two, pulse eighty-six, temperature thirty-six point eight. That's grand. I'll call the doctor.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good morning, Mr Brennan. I'm Dr Keane. What can I do for you?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. It is my right big toe. It became extremely painful during the night, and this morning it is quite swollen.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He hardly got a wink. Shifting about in the bed from about two.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry to hear it. Did it start yesterday evening, or only after you'd gone to bed?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I went to bed quite comfortable. I woke around one, perhaps half past, and the toe was already throbbing.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): How bad is the pain, if you were to give it a number?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, I ought to say that I take a water tablet. Bendroflumethiazide, two point five milligrams every morning, for my blood pressure. I have been on it some years.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll come to the tablet shortly. On the pain itself, how severe is it just now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): It is very severe, Doctor. I can scarcely set the foot to the floor. I should say eight, perhaps nine.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): And is there redness, or is it the swelling and the pain mainly?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): It is red across the joint, and warm to the touch. My wife noticed the heat.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Burning hot, it was, when I felt it before we came out.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chance you knocked it, or stubbed the toe?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. I cannot recall an injury.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, that isn't accurate. I did kick the leg of the kitchen chair yesterday evening. I made nothing of it at the time.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): So there was a small knock. Did the pain come on straight after that?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I walked about afterwards with no difficulty at all. The bad pain only came in the night.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has this happened to you before?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. About a year back, the same toe. It settled after a few days.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was very sorry for himself. Missed a whole weekend of golf, but it did pass.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me set it out as I understand it. Very painful, red, swollen right big toe since last night; you kicked a chair yesterday evening but walked fine afterwards; and a similar episode about a year ago that settled in a few days.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. That is correct.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Besides the bendroflumethiazide, do you take any other medicine?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only that, two point five milligrams each morning.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has a pint or two of beer at the weekends, though. More if there's a match on.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much beer would that be, would you say?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Two pints, sometimes three, on a Saturday. I do not drink through the week. I keep to that.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I won't run through every other system. Let me examine the toe.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): The right big toe is swollen and red over the joint, and it's tender when I press. The other toes are clear, and the skin isn't broken.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): This has the look of gout, an acute attack in the big toe joint. I can't be certain without the blood test, but that is my working impression, particularly with the water tablet and the beer at weekends.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I had wondered if it might be gout, after the last time.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd like your blood uric acid checked. The nurse can take it before you go.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I'll do it on the way out. No bother.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): We can treat this with colchicine, or with an anti-inflammatory such as naproxen. As you're on a diuretic, I'd sooner start with colchicine.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I have no trouble with my stomach, Doctor, but I am content to take your advice.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then colchicine, five hundred micrograms twice a day, for five days. If it causes diarrhoea, stop it and we can switch to naproxen, five hundred milligrams twice a day with food, only if the colchicine doesn't suit you.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day for five days. I understand.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should he stay off the beer in the meantime? The car park was desperate, by the way; we were circling for twenty minutes.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): No beer until this settles, and I'd advise cutting back at the weekends after that. Keep the foot raised, and ice wrapped in a cloth for about ten minutes at a time is fine. Continue the bendroflumethiazide as usual until we see the uric acid.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back if it is not easing in three days, or sooner if the redness spreads or you feel unwell. Otherwise I'll see you next week with the result.

omissions.text: Pain severity was rated 8 to 9 out of 10, and he could scarcely put the foot to the floor.
Pain onset detail: he went to bed comfortable and woke around 1 to 1:30 am with the toe already throbbing.
Denied recalled injury initially, then corrected himself that he had kicked the leg of a kitchen chair the previous evening; this was a real correction in the history.
After kicking the chair, he walked about afterwards with no difficulty at all.
Examination finding missing/wrongly recorded: tenderness was when pressing over the right big toe joint; the recorded fact says tenderness of the right big toe more generally.
Doctor stated he could not be certain it was gout without the blood test; gout was a working impression rather than confirmed diagnosis.
Important conditional adverse-effect instruction missing: if colchicine causes diarrhoea, stop it.
